1. What is the primary characteristic of a monolithic application architecture?

A. Each business functionality runs as an independent service
B. All major application components are packaged and deployed as a single application
C. The frontend and database must run on separate cloud platforms
D. Every module requires an independent database

2. Which of the following is a major advantage of distributed application architecture over monolithic architecture?

A. All components must be deployed together
B. Independent services can be developed, deployed, and scaled separately
C. Network communication is completely eliminated
D. Database management is no longer required

3. A banking application contains customer management, account management, and transaction processing within a single deployable Spring Boot application. Which architecture does this represent?

A. Microservices architecture
B. Monolithic architecture
C. Serverless architecture
D. Peer-to-peer architecture

4. In a typical Spring Boot web application, which component is primarily responsible for handling HTTP requests from clients?

A. Repository
B. Controller
C. Entity
D. Database

5. What is the primary responsibility of the frontend in a client-server application?

A. To manage database transactions directly
B. To provide the user interface and interact with backend services
C. To execute database stored procedures
D. To configure the backend dependency injection container

6. Which statement best describes the relationship between frontend, backend, and database?

A. The frontend stores all business data, while the database manages user interfaces
B. The frontend interacts with the backend, and the backend handles business logic and database operations
C. The database directly manages frontend navigation
D. The backend is responsible only for displaying HTML pages

7. In client-server architecture, what is the responsibility of the client?

A. To provide requests for services or resources from the server
B. To manage all server-side business logic
C. To maintain the server's database schema
D. To configure server application deployment

8. Which HTTP method is generally used to retrieve information from a REST API?

A. POST
B. DELETE
C. GET
D. PATCH

9. A Spring Boot application exposes /api/customers to allow external applications to retrieve customer information. What does this endpoint represent?

A. A database table
B. A REST API resource endpoint
C. A Java package
D. A Maven plugin

10. What is the primary purpose of REST-based application architecture?

A. To enable communication between systems through standardized HTTP-based interfaces
B. To eliminate the need for a backend
C. To allow only Java applications to communicate
D. To replace relational databases with Java classes

11. A company wants to scale its payment processing functionality independently without scaling its entire application. Which architecture is more suitable?

A. Monolithic architecture
B. Distributed or microservices architecture
C. Single-tier architecture
D. Standalone desktop architecture

12. What is a major challenge associated with distributed application architecture?

A. It cannot support independent deployment
B. It introduces network communication, service coordination, and distributed failure-handling complexity
C. It does not support REST APIs
D. It requires all services to use the same programming language

13. In Spring Boot, what is the primary purpose of the embedded Tomcat server in a typical web application?

A. To manage database schemas
B. To receive and process incoming HTTP requests through the web application
C. To compile Java source files
D. To manage Maven dependencies

14. A mobile application needs to retrieve product details from a Spring Boot backend. Which communication approach is most appropriate?

A. Directly accessing the backend's Java objects
B. Calling a REST API using an HTTP request
C. Reading the backend's Maven configuration
D. Accessing the server's local Java memory

15. A Spring Boot application is divided into separate layers for controllers, services, and repositories but is deployed as one executable JAR. Which statement is correct?

A. It must be a microservices application because it has multiple layers
B. It can be a layered monolithic application
C. It is necessarily a distributed application
D. It cannot use Spring MVC

16. What is the primary objective of the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern?

A. To combine database operations and user interface code into a single class
B. To separate application responsibilities into Model, View, and Controller components
C. To eliminate the need for backend processing
D. To replace object-oriented programming

17. In MVC architecture, what is the primary responsibility of the Model?

A. To manage application data and related business state
B. To receive HTTP requests directly from the browser
C. To display HTML pages
D. To configure the web server

18. Which component in MVC is primarily responsible for presenting information to the user?

A. Controller
B. Repository
C. View
D. Service

19. What is the primary responsibility of the Controller in Spring MVC?

A. To directly manage physical database storage
B. To receive incoming requests, invoke appropriate processing, and return responses
C. To define HTML page styling
D. To compile Java source code

20. Which Spring MVC annotation is commonly used to define a controller that returns data directly as the HTTP response body?

A. @Entity
B. @Repository
C. @RestController
D. @Autowired

21. What is the difference between @Controller and @RestController in Spring MVC?

A. @Controller is used only for database operations
B. @RestController combines @Controller and @ResponseBody behavior
C. @Controller automatically creates database tables
D. Both annotations are used exclusively for service classes

22. In a traditional Spring MVC application, what does a controller generally return when using server-side view rendering?

A. A database connection
B. A view name that is resolved by the view resolver
C. A Maven dependency
D. A Java compiler instruction

23. What is the purpose of the @RequestMapping annotation in Spring MVC?

A. To map HTTP requests to controller classes or methods
B. To define database table relationships
C. To create Java constructors automatically
D. To configure Maven build phases

24. Which annotation is specifically designed to map HTTP GET requests to controller methods?

A. @PostMapping
B. @PutMapping
C. @GetMapping
D. @DeleteMapping

25. Consider the following Spring Boot controller method:
@GetMapping("/products")
public List<Product> getProducts() {
    return productService.findAll();
}


What is the primary responsibility of this controller method?

A. To directly execute SQL statements
B. To handle GET requests and delegate product retrieval to the service layer
C. To create the Product database table
D. To configure the Maven build lifecycle

26. In a traditional Spring MVC request-response flow, which component selects and resolves the appropriate view after controller processing?

A. DispatcherServlet and ViewResolver
B. EntityManager only
C. Maven Compiler Plugin
D. JDBC Driver Manager

27. What is the role of the DispatcherServlet in Spring MVC?

A. To act as the front controller that receives and dispatches incoming HTTP requests
B. To execute SQL queries directly
C. To generate Java bytecode
D. To manage Git repositories

28. A developer places database query logic directly inside a Spring MVC controller. Which design principle is most likely being violated?

A. Separation of concerns
B. Encapsulation only
C. Method overloading
D. Inheritance

29. Why is it recommended to separate the Model, View, and Controller responsibilities?

A. To increase dependency between application components
B. To improve maintainability, testability, and separation of concerns
C. To eliminate all Java classes
D. To avoid using HTTP requests

30. A Spring Boot REST application uses @RestController and returns a Java object from a method. What generally happens to the returned object?

A. It is automatically converted into an HTTP response body, commonly JSON through an HTTP message converter
B. It is automatically stored in a database table
C. It is converted into a Maven dependency
D. It is displayed as a server-side JSP page by default

31. In a typical Spring Boot REST application, which component receives an incoming HTTP request first within the Spring MVC request-processing mechanism?

A. Service class
B. Repository interface
C. DispatcherServlet
D. Entity class

32. After DispatcherServlet receives an incoming request, which component is responsible for identifying the appropriate controller method?

A. HandlerMapping
B. EntityManager
C. JdbcTemplate
D. Maven Compiler

33. What is the primary responsibility of a Spring Boot Controller in a layered application?

A. To handle HTTP requests and delegate business operations to the service layer
B. To execute all database queries directly
C. To manage database connection pooling
D. To configure the application's Maven dependencies

34. Which Spring annotation is commonly used to identify a service-layer class?

A. @Entity
B. @Service
C. @RestController
D. @Table

35. What is the primary responsibility of the Service layer in a Spring Boot application?

A. To handle HTTP request routing only
B. To implement business logic and coordinate application operations
C. To generate HTML pages
D. To manage application server ports

36. Which annotation is commonly used to identify a Spring Data access component?

A. @Repository
B. @ControllerAdvice
C. @RequestBody
D. @ConfigurationProperties

37. What is the primary responsibility of the Repository layer?

A. To handle frontend navigation
B. To manage data access and database-related operations
C. To validate HTTP response status codes only
D. To configure API endpoints

38. Consider the following request flow:

Client → Controller → Service → Repository → Database.

Which layer should normally contain the business rule that prevents a customer from withdrawing more money than the available account balance?

A. Controller
B. Service
C. Repository
D. Database connection driver

39. Which Spring annotation is used to indicate that a method should execute within a database transaction?

A. @RequestMapping
B. @Transactional
C. @GetMapping
D. @ResponseBody

40. What is the primary advantage of using dependency injection in Spring Boot?

A. It eliminates the need for Java objects
B. It reduces tight coupling by allowing Spring to provide required dependencies
C. It automatically converts SQL into Java code
D. It prevents all runtime exceptions

41. In a Spring Boot REST API, which annotation is commonly used to bind incoming JSON request data to a Java object?

A. @RequestParam
B. @PathVariable
C. @RequestBody
D. @ResponseStatus

42. Consider the following endpoint:
@GetMapping("/customers/{id}")
public Customer getCustomer(@PathVariable Long id) {
    return customerService.findById(id);
}


What is the purpose of @PathVariable?

A. To retrieve a value from the URL path and bind it to a method parameter
B. To retrieve data from the HTTP request body
C. To connect directly to the database
D. To configure the service-layer transaction

43. A client sends a POST request containing customer details in JSON format. Which combination is most appropriate for processing this request in Spring Boot?

A. @GetMapping and @PathVariable
B. @PostMapping and @RequestBody
C. @DeleteMapping and @ResponseBody
D. @PutMapping and @Entity

44. What is the purpose of ResponseEntity in Spring Boot?

A. To represent an HTTP response with control over status code, headers, and response body
B. To create a database connection
C. To manage Java object inheritance
D. To define Maven project dependencies

45. A repository method returns Optional<Customer>. What is the main advantage of using Optional in this situation?

A. It guarantees that the customer exists
B. It represents the possible absence of a customer and encourages explicit handling
C. It automatically creates a new customer if none exists
D. It converts the customer object into JSON

46. Which Spring mechanism is commonly used to handle exceptions globally across multiple REST controllers?

A. @ComponentScan
B. @ControllerAdvice or @RestControllerAdvice
C. @EntityScan
D. @EnableScheduling

47. A Spring Boot API receives a request for a customer ID that does not exist in the database. Which HTTP status code is generally appropriate for the resulting resource-not-found response?

A. 200 OK
B. 201 Created
C. 404 Not Found
D. 500 Internal Server Error

48. A service method performs two database updates within one transaction. The second update fails. What should normally happen when the transaction is rolled back?

A. The first update remains permanently committed
B. Both updates are rolled back as part of the same transaction
C. The entire database is deleted
D. Only the failed Java method is removed

49. Consider the following Spring Boot request flow:
Client
  ↓
Controller
  ↓
Service
  ↓
Repository
  ↓
Database


The application returns an incorrect customer balance even though the repository retrieves the correct database record. Which layer should be investigated first?

A. Frontend browser rendering only
B. Service layer business calculations and transformations
C. Maven dependency download process
D. DispatcherServlet configuration only

50. A Spring Boot application receives a REST request, validates input, executes business logic, accesses the database, and returns a JSON response. Which sequence best represents the typical request-processing flow?

A. Client → Repository → Database → Controller → Service → Response
B. Client → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service → Repository → Database → Response
C. Client → Database → Service → Repository → Controller → Response
D. Client → Service → Database → DispatcherServlet → Repository → Response
